claims.text: The current intermediate layer is a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy such as WMoTaNb without CNT addition.
The proposed intervention is to add 1–3 wt.% surface-functionalized CNTs to the HEA powder before spark plasma sintering.
Mild oxidation or silanization can be used to surface-functionalize the CNTs.
SPS under optimized temperature and pressure will produce homogeneous CNT dispersion and strong CNT–matrix interfacial bonding.
Surface-functionalized CNTs will form a coherent, uniformly distributed network in the refractory HEA.
The CNT network will chemically bond to the HEA matrix.
The CNT network will reinforce grain boundaries.
The CNT network will provide interconnected pathways for rapid heat transfer.
CNTs have intrinsic thermal conductivity greater than 3000 W/m·K.
The high intrinsic thermal conductivity of CNTs will create effective nanoscale heat-conduction channels in the HEA composite.
CNT surface functionalization will promote strong chemical interaction and interfacial bonding with the refractory HEA matrix.
Strong CNT–matrix bonding will maintain microstructural integrity and mitigate stress concentrations during cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
The CNT-doped HEA will have significantly higher effective thermal conductivity than the CNT-free baseline.
The increased effective thermal conductivity will enhance heat dissipation.
CNT addition will preserve or only minimally affect yield strength under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
CNT addition will preserve or only minimally affect fracture toughness under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
The CNT-free tungsten-based refractory HEA baseline has limited thermal conductivity relative to the proposed CNT composite.
The proposed benefits will persist during cyclic thermal shocks up to approximately 1000°C with relevant mechanical loading.
Oxidation or other plasma-induced reactions may degrade the functionalized CNTs and reduce performance during prolonged exposure.
